entries.author: mike
entries.summary: Created branch bugfix/remove-stackable-loot-exclusion off main and executed all 3 plan steps with no deviations.
entries.detail: LootAlertListener.java:99 - removed '!composition.isStackable()' from the value-check condition, leaving just 'config.lootSharingEnabled()'. Updated the class Javadoc to describe the LOOT check as applying to any item's total stack value, stackable or not, rather than 'any single non-stackable drop'. ./gradlew.bat compileJava -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Only warning is the pre-existing, already-tracked deprecated-ItemID note (WRN-008), unrelated to this change.

entries.author: mike
entries.summary: Task abandoned during verification - reverted the stackable-exclusion removal, keeping the original !composition.isStackable() guard.
entries.detail: During verify-task, developer reconsidered: the confirmed root cause of the original Yama report (a real drop not alerting) turned out to be an Oathplate armour piece - non-stackable, ~82m gp, well above the 1.5m threshold - so the stackable exclusion was never actually the cause in that case, and is likely already resolved by consolidate-loot-listeners' LootReceived/EVENT-type fix instead. Decided to keep the original non-stackable-only value check as-is (it still serves its original purpose of filtering noisy routine stackable drops) rather than loosen it on a hypothetical (Oathplate shards) that wasn't the real incident. LootAlertListener.java reverted to exactly match main (confirmed via git diff, no changes remain). No code shipped from this task.
